articles.title: Howard Stern and wife Beth turned the loss of their dog Bianca into an animal-rescue legacy; a 14,000-square-foot cat adoption centre now operates in her name, and Beth has helped rehome over 2,000 cats since 2013
articles.summary: The death of a much-loved English bulldog in 2012 set radio host Howard Stern and his wife, Beth Stern, on a journey that would change animal rescue
articles.body: The death of a much-loved English bulldog in 2012 set radio host Howard Stern and his wife, Beth Stern, on a journey that would change animal rescue efforts across the United States. After their dog Bianca passed away, the couple turned their sadness into a nationwide fundraising campaign with North Shore Animal League America. Their efforts led to the creation of Bianca's Furry Friends Feline Adoption Center, a 14,000-square-foot facility on the second floor of the organisation's campus in Port Washington, New York. Since becoming directly involved with North Shore Animal League America as a volunteer foster parent in 2013, Beth Stern has personally cared for and helped find homes for more than 2,000 rescued cats and kittens, according to official records published by the organisation.Building a state-of-the-art rescue hubBianca's Furry Friends Feline Adoption Center opened after a major fundraising campaign led by the Stern family. The centre was designed to give shelter cats a better place to live while waiting to be adopted. According to North Shore Animal League America, the 14,000-square-foot facility has open, cage-free rooms where cats can move around freely instead of being kept in traditional metal cages. Large windows stretching from floor to ceiling let in natural sunlight. Special climbing walls, raised platforms, and small spaces for cats to hide and rest also help keep the animals active and comfortable. The new centre allowed North Shore Animal League America to double the number of cats it could rescue and care for on campus. Moving the cats to the new upper-floor facility also freed up a large amount of space on the ground floor of the main building. This allowed the organisation to take in more rescued dogs and puppies. The facility also has a separate medical room, a surgery room, a nursery for nursing mothers, and special isolation rooms for animals recovering from infectious diseases or operations.From personal grief to hands-on fosteringThe idea for the adoption centre came from the couple's close bond with their bulldog, Bianca, who was often mentioned on Howard Stern's radio show. After Bianca died, Beth Stern began focusing much of her public work on directly helping animals in need. As a spokesperson and volunteer foster parent for North Shore Animal League America, Beth uses the couple's home in New York as a temporary shelter for animals that need extra attention and medical care. "Fostering is the most rewarding thing I have ever done in my life," Beth Stern said in a profile published by North Shore Animal League America. "Taking in an animal that is sick, scared, or neglected, nursing them back to health, and then finding them a loving forever home is an incredible experience." Her fostering work mainly focuses on animals that are especially vulnerable. These include newborn orphaned kittens that need bottle feeding around the clock, pregnant cats, and animals suffering from physical injuries or serious medical conditions.Broadening public support and adoption eventsAlong with fostering animals and helping develop the adoption centre, the Sterns use public events to raise money and awareness for shelters that do not put healthy or treatable animals down. Beth Stern hosts major national animal welfare programmes, including the annual Kitten Bowl on the Great American Family channel. The event is organised in partnership with North Shore Animal League America and aims to encourage people across the country to adopt shelter animals. The attention brought by Bianca's Furry Friends has also helped increase adoption efforts across the region. North Shore Animal League America, which is recognised as the world's largest no-kill rescue and adoption organisation, reports that it has saved more than 1.1 million animal lives since it was founded in 1944. Howard Stern also regularly talks about the adoption centre's work on The Howard Stern Show on SiriusXM. He encourages listeners to consider adopting animals, volunteering at shelters, or becoming foster parents.Operational expansion and specialized careHaving a separate cat facility allows medical staff at North Shore Animal League America to provide special treatment for serious feline illnesses. These include upper respiratory infections and ringworm. Such conditions can sometimes lead traditional municipal shelters to euthanise affected animals. Bianca's Furry Friends has separate quarantine rooms where veterinary teams can treat sick cats without putting other animals in the shelter at risk of infection. The adoption centre also has special meeting rooms where people interested in adopting can spend time with cats in a comfortable, home-like setting before completing the adoption process. Beth Stern continues to take in groups of rescued kittens throughout the year. She regularly shares updates about their recovery and development on her social media accounts. articles.summary: Mexican television presenter Ines Gomez Mont, who once made headlines for asking NFL legend Tom Brady to marry her, has been arrested in Miami after
articles.body: Mexican television presenter Ines Gomez Mont, who once made headlines for asking NFL legend Tom Brady to marry her, has been arrested in Miami after spending nearly five years outside Mexico amid a massive fraud investigation. The 43-year-old was detained by US authorities on October 30, 2026, in connection with allegations of organised crime, money laundering and tax fraud.According to Mexican news agency reports and Mexico's Attorney General's Office (FGR), Gomez Mont is accused of being part of an alleged criminal network that siphoned public money through a series of bogus companies and fraudulent invoices. Her lawyer husband, Victor Manuel Alvarez Puga, is also accused of being involved in the operation, which investigators estimate involved around 2.95 billion pesos, or approximately £120 million.The former television host was reportedly taken into custody in Miami, Florida, where she was photographed being escorted by police officers in handcuffs. She is currently in US custody, pending immigration proceedings and any formal extradition process to Mexico.Ines Gomez Mont and husband fled Mexico in 2021Gomez Mont and Alvarez Puga left Mexico with their family in September 2021 after arrest warrants were issued against them over the alleged financial scam. The couple had remained outside the country as Mexican authorities continued their investigation.Their arrest comes weeks after Interpol reportedly withdrew the international red notices against the pair in September 2026. Despite the removal of the notices, the arrest warrants issued in Mexico remained active.Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum had criticised Interpol's decision and maintained that her government would continue seeking the couple's extradition. Mexican prosecutors said the presenter's arrest followed an exchange of information between Mexican and US authorities.According to reports, Mexican investigators had located the couple in Miami as early as 2022. However, a formal extradition request was not made until December 2025.What are the allegations against the TV presenter?Investigators allege that the couple were connected to a network of companies that issued fraudulent invoices and created contracts for services that were never actually delivered. The money was allegedly routed through multiple bank transactions to conceal its origin.The alleged operation is said to have involved funds from Mexico's Ministry of the Interior during the presidency of Enrique Pena Nieto. At least 18 million pesos reportedly ended up in bank accounts belonging to Gomez Mont and her husband.Alvarez Puga, who has been dubbed the 'King of the Invoice Mills', is accused of masterminding the alleged operation. Investigators have also linked him to a network of contacts involving politicians, former government officials, lawyers, businesspeople and celebrities.The lawyer was reportedly detained by US immigration officers in Miami in 2025 over irregularities concerning his stay in the country. He was subsequently released, and his current whereabouts remain unclear.President Sheinbaum has previously accused the couple of being involved in fraudulent invoicing. She has also called for cooperation from Washington, pointing to Mexico's transfer of around 100 prisoners wanted by the Trump administration to the United States.Ines Gomez Mont has maintained her innocenceGomez Mont has denied the allegations since the case came to light. In October 2021, shortly after the warrants were issued, she addressed the controversy in a statement shared with her 2.5 million Instagram followers.She said she had faith that the truth would emerge and that her innocence would be established. Calling the allegations an injustice, she insisted that she would continue to speak out despite what she described as attempts to silence her.The presenter has not been convicted of the alleged offences. The allegations against her and her husband remain subject to legal proceedings.Ines Gomez Mont once asked Tom Brady to marry herApart from her television career and the ongoing fraud case, Gomez Mont was also known internationally for an unusual moment involving former NFL quarterback Tom Brady.During the 2008 Super Bowl, while reporting on the event, she famously asked Brady to marry her. The football star turned down the proposal, making the exchange a memorable moment from her time covering the sporting event.Years later, the presenter has again made international headlines, this time following her arrest in the United States over the allegations linked to the multi-million-pound fraud investigation.You use AI every day. articles.title: Now kids want to know why they are learning something, says Inventure Academy’s Nooraine Fazal
articles.summary: Nooraine Fazal of Inventure Academy on Bengaluru’s change, kids’ learning shift to “why,” experiential education, less sport, and giving children freedom.
articles.body: Best Of Ooru | Nooraine Fazal is founder, CEO and managing trustee of Bengaluru-based school chain Inventure Academy, established in 2005. An educationist, entrepreneur and former Karnataka women’s cricket and basketball player, she holds an MS in Management from Boston UniversityYou’ve lived and worked in several cities abroad. What did you miss most about Bengaluru—and what surprised you when you returned?What I missed most about Bengaluru varied depending on when and where I lived. When I was in London (1991–93), it was just about everything, starting with people and food! It took me a while to come to terms with the fact that I had chosen to leave India to learn more about the world, and myself.While living in the desert sands of Dubai and Abu Dhabi, it was Bengaluru’s greenery and weather that I missed most.What surprised me most when I returned was how much Bengaluru had transformed. It had been my small, friendly city, where I couldn’t move an inch without my parents somehow finding out where I was (this was pre-mobile era!). I returned to a larger, bustling IT city that was home to people from across India, and increasingly, expats.As much as I loved Bengaluru’s new energy and diversity, I was disheartened to see a city racing ahead in growth while falling behind in livability — its lakes and greenery giving way to concrete and glass structures, and its public infrastructure struggling to keep pace.You represented Karnataka in cricket and basketball. Which Bengaluru grounds and courts shaped you?My sporting journey began on the fields of Clarence High School—one on campus, the other 2–3 km away on Assaye Road. Getting to the latter was an adventure in itself! We walked or cycled, crossed railway tracks on foot, and then cleaned the field before marking it for Sports Day. Can’t imagine middle- or upper-middle-class school kids being required by the school to do that today—would probably make for a viral post or two on social media!It was on those fields that I discovered my potential as a sportsperson. I had just joined Clarence and very quickly found myself selected as the school hockey goalkeeper. All of 11 years old (and pretty short then!), I was keeping goal for the senior school team, with cricket pads, fast reflexes and lots of courage (or was that stupidity?!) as my armour.And then, of course, came Mount Carmel (which I absolutely loved for the sports and leadership opportunities), KSCA, IISc, Kanteerava, MICO, and the courts at Malleswaram and Jayanagar.Sport took me across Bengaluru and India—and, thankfully, out of the classroom, where we were generally expected to sit quietly, take notes and memorise them for the year-end exam!Where do you go when you want an unhurried afternoon in the city?Nandi Hills! It was my favourite getaway growing up. I cycled there as a pre-teen and graduated to a motorcycle as a teenager (err, yes, I may have been underage!). And it remains a favourite to this day.Which Bengaluru dish would you happily cross the city for?Mom’s Kutchi Biryani — by far the best in the world! (And anyone who has tasted it will vouch for that!) No restaurant in Bengaluru comes close. And I do cross from the Republic of Whitefield to head to my parents home in Fraser Town regularly for it!From Gen Z to Gen Alpha, what changes do you see in the way Bengaluru’s children think and learn?Children increasingly want to know why they’re learning something. What’s the relevance? Why memorise what they can look up in seconds?There’s a greater appetite for hands-on, experiential and project-based learning, and for exploring interests beyond academics, particularly the arts. They’re also spending far more time online—learning, creating, connecting and, yes, playing video games!At the same time, they’re increasingly competitive, with getting admission into a great college seen as the pathway to success. Their lives are packed with tuitions, activity classes and organised schedules, leaving little time for spontaneous play and informal learning.What worries me is that children have fewer opportunities to navigate friendships, disagreements and failures without adult intervention. That’s where so much social-emotional learning happens!As a former sportsperson, I also worry that children play far less sport. There’s perhaps more interest in being fit, and looking fit, but that’s very different from playing on a team, learning to win and lose, working hard together, and simply having fun.Of course, neither generation is homogeneous. These shifts also reflect the environments we, as parents, educators and society, have created.Less memorisation, more questioning and learning by doing is welcome. But at what cost to independence and learning from life beyond the classroom?Is there a message on early learning that you’d like to share with young parents?Let your children be children!Give them the freedom to explore, experiment and mess up sometimes, with a safety net and sensible guardrails, rather than trying to protect them from every disappointment or difficulty.Some of my biggest learnings came from the streets and playing fields of Bengaluru. From dealing with bullying, a teacher who simply didn’t believe in me (more than compensated for by those who did—so yes, you win some, you lose some!), friendships and heartbreaks, success and failure, and even discord at home.These experiences taught me to shut out the noise, find my own voice and recognise that life isn’t always black and white. It’s often about finding the right shade of grey, learning to understand and respect different perspectives and ways of being, without necessarily agreeing with them, and recognising that there are many pathways to success.Children need love, trust and guidance, but also the space to figure things out for themselves. We can’t live their lives for them, nor should we try to.After all, isn’t growing up about so much more than learning to read, write and count? It’s about learning to navigate life!You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Five months after news broke of pilferage of donations at Ayodhya Ram temple, Supreme Court cleared trial of eight people, who figure in the chargesheet filed by the SIT for allegedly siphoning Rs 2.7 crore. It also gave the petitioners, who had sought probe, the status of victims of crime and allowed them to assist in the trial, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.The SIT's status report informed SC that financial and forensic examination extended to cash deposits, transactions, property purchases, construction expenditure, vehicles, jewellery, other assets, and event-related spendings. "The amount of alleged embezzlement is approximately Rs 2.7 crore," the report said.On Monday, solicitor general Tushar Mehta explained to the court the process that involved scrutiny of bank accounts and acquisition of immoveable properties by the accused, as well as examination of CCTV footage that culminated in the chargesheet Sept 23.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the trial court to proceed with the trial in accordance with law. On the large number of petitioners who had sought an independent probe into the donation theft, the bench said the petitioners can be given the status of victims of crime, and in public interest, they can assist the prosecutor and trial court in proceedings.One of the petitioners also sought a direction from SC for an “independent, impartial, technically competent survey/demarcation” of the land that was allotted for the temple by SC in its Nov 9, 2019, judgement.He also sought a direction to the revenue and statutory authorities to place before SC relevant records and their comparison with the site plan and actual location of the Ram Janmabhoomi Temple complex to determine if the present complex stands on the land allotted by the court.While Mehta said it is impermissible for the petitioner to seek a virtual reopening of the judgement by a fivejudge bench, the bench said if the petitioner had any grievance about the demarcation of the land, he should approach the civil court with a civil suit.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Paris Hilton launched a recovery fund for women-owned businesses after disasters; a year after her Los Angeles wildfire grants, 90% of recipient businesses were still operating
articles.summary: When natural disasters destroy homes and neighbourhoods, small businesses can face a difficult recovery of their own.
articles.body: When natural disasters destroy homes and neighbourhoods, small businesses can face a difficult recovery of their own. For women who depend on those businesses to support their families, losing a workplace can also mean losing a source of income and the livelihoods of employees. Paris Hilton has launched a new initiative aimed at helping women business owners facing that situation across the US. As reported by The Associated Press, the Back in Business Recovery Fund follows a programme she supported after the 2025 Los Angeles wildfires, when grants helped dozens of businesses deal with the immediate costs of rebuilding.Paris Hilton commits $350,000 to new recovery fundHilton has pledged $350,000 to establish the Back in Business Recovery Fund, which aims to raise at least $1 million by the end of March. The initiative is being run through her social impact organisation, 11:11 Media Impact, in partnership with GoFundMe.org, the charitable arm of the fundraising platform. GoFundMe.org is contributing a further $100,000 towards the launch, according to The Associated Press reports.The programme is intended to reach women who own small businesses affected by disasters across the country. Rather than being limited to one type of emergency or a particular industry, it is designed to provide financial assistance when businesses are struggling to reopen or maintain operations after a damaging event.Hilton said her involvement came partly from seeing how much locally owned businesses contribute to the communities around them. She also wanted to extend the work beyond Los Angeles, where she had previously helped provide financial support to business owners affected by the fires.Paris Hilton's earlier wildfire fund helped businesses cover rent, wages and rebuilding costsThe new fund builds on a programme Hilton backed following the January 2025 wildfires in Los Angeles. The fires destroyed her Malibu home, where she had been raising her young children, and left many other residents facing the loss of their properties and livelihoods.In the aftermath, Hilton's organisation and GoFundMe.org distributed more than $1 million in grants to 50 women-owned small businesses. Individual awards reached up to $25,000, with recipients using the money for expenses including rent, staff wages, replacement equipment and rebuilding damaged premises.Among those helped were owners of childcare centres, bakeries, bookshops, dance studios and beauty salons. Many of the businesses had been affected by the Eaton fire, which caused extensive destruction in Altadena.For Hilton, the experience of losing her own home brought the financial difficulties facing other mothers into sharper focus. Renata Ortega told The Associated Press, “Nothing prepares you for that amount of loss.”90% of Los Angeles grant recipients were still operating a year laterA year after the grants were distributed, 90% of the recipient businesses remained in operation, according to the Pasadena Women's Business Center reported by The Associated Press. The organisation also received funding to offer technical support and mentoring to businesses affected by the fires.For some owners, the grants helped meet costs that might otherwise have prevented them from reopening, while others were able to replace equipment or secure premises from which to continue trading. Renata Ortega, owner of Orla Floral Studio, was among the recipients. She had operated her floral design business from a converted garage beside her home in Altadena, where she lived with her husband and three dogs. The Eaton fire destroyed the property, including her studio and the equipment she had accumulated over several years.The loss left her uncertain about whether she could continue the business. She was also concerned about the people whose income depended on her work, including her employees and flower market suppliers.The grant helped Ortega put down a deposit on a new studio and buy a replacement floral cooler. Those purchases allowed her to resume operations without losing her existing staff. She said the business had since become busy again and that she was considering taking on another employee.Hilton continued supporting businesses after the grantsHilton's involvement with some of the Los Angeles recipients extended beyond the initial financial assistance. Reportedly, she became a customer of several businesses, wearing a catsuit from clothing retailer Crop It Like It's Hot at the Coachella music festival and bringing local food vendors, including Carmela Ice Cream and Hot Shrimp Mami, to her events.Hilton, the great-granddaughter of hotel magnate Conrad N. Hilton, also spoke about being underestimated during her career. She said she had worked to establish herself as more than the public image many people associated with her.According to Wells Fargo figures cited in the announcement, the US has 14.5 million women-owned businesses, representing 39% of all businesses. Yet women, particularly those from minority communities, continue to receive a smaller share of venture capital and loan funding than men.Rebecca Grone, director of 11:11 Media Impact, said women business owners often have fewer financial resources available to them. Those with primary responsibility for caring for children or other family members can also face additional pressures when trying to recover after a disaster.Women's business centres will help identify grant recipientsThe Back in Business Recovery Fund will work with some of the approximately 150 women's business centres operating across the US. These organisations are expected to help identify business owners affected by disasters and connect them with financial assistance.The grants will be unrestricted, allowing recipients to decide how best to use the money for their businesses. The approach follows the Los Angeles programme, where owners were able to direct funding towards immediate operating costs, equipment and other needs.Amanda Brown Lierman, executive director of GoFundMe.org, said, “Collaborating with the centers will help identify impacted women quickly and opens up access not just to cash, but to a community of business owners facing similar challenges.”The timing of the fund's activation will depend partly on assessments from these centres. They will help establish where assistance is needed and when the programme should respond.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Secondary school teacher to Fair Isle crofter - life on the UK's most remote island
articles.summary: Katy Phenix relocated to Fair Isle from Redcar in North Yorkshire with her partner Josh Moore and their children Teddy, 11, and Hetty, six.
articles.body:
Katy Phenix's new life as a crofter on the UK's most remote inhabited island is a far cry from her previous life as a history teacher in a secondary school.

The 33-year-old relocated to Fair Isle from Redcar, North Yorkshire, with her partner Josh Moore, 35, and their children Teddy, 11, and Hetty, six, in July.

They had never visited the island before moving there but were seeking more family time and a better quality of life.

Four months on, they say they have settled in to their "completely different" island life and feel "really lucky".

Fair Isle lies half-way between Orkney and Shetland and has a population of about 60 people.

It is three-miles (5km) long and owned by the National Trust for Scotland (NTS).

Since moving to the island, Katy has begun working as a part-time crofter - a crofter is a person who shares pasture land to raise livestock.

She said the family mainly moved to Fair Isle for more time together.

"We weren't living the lives we wanted," she said. "We were snatching time together over weekends and holidays.

"You get a mortgage, you get a car and you have to work to keep that up. Moving to Fair Isle has cut all of that out."

Fair Isle has a primary school and nursery, a local shop, post office and a community hall.

Katy has also taken up a post in early years education.

Her children are two of only five pupils at the local primary school.

Josh is in high demand as a self-employed electrician because Fair Isle is off-grid with its own energy system.

The island's homes are powered by a combination of wind and solar power.

A diesel generator provides a back-up supply.

Josh is working on a large battery replacement project.

"We're switching to new lithium ones," he said. "I'm also fixing people's lights and sockets."

He said friends and family had been supportive of the family's move.

The couple have been engaged for several years and are planning a wedding on the island in 2027.

"The church is literally next door", Katy said.

The pair said they hoped another family with children would move to Fair Isle early next year.

The National Trust for Scotland has advertised a further opportunity, with a five-bedroom house and 12-acre (5ha) croft available to rent.

The trust said it was encouraging applicants with crofting and land management experience, trade skills such as plumbing or anyone looking to develop a craft business on the island.

Angus Murray, NTS operations manager for Fair Isle, said: "We're inviting applications from hard-working and enthusiastic people who will bring skills, creativity and care to this special place."

The deadline for applications is Sunday 8 November.

Eileen Thomson, who chairs the Fair Isle committee, said everyone had a role to play.

"You'll see people working in the fire service, the shop and the school," she said.

Eileen said the new tenants should be multi-skilled.

"A lot of the really big jobs need every single person to turn up and help, whether it's gathering all the common grazing sheep or doing the hay bales in summer," she added.

She said creative people could also support the famous Fair Isle knitwear - a textile developed on the island in the early 19th Century.

Eleven-year-old Teddy hopes more children will move to the island so he can start a football team.

"We do a lot of outdoor activity," he said.

His six-year-old sister Hetty added that their seven pets from North Yorkshire were "loving" island life.

articles.title: Prince William apologises after backlash over 3,000-acre Bradninch Estate sale; tenants demand fair valuations, King Charles disappointed as Duchy of Cornwall faces capital gains tax questions
articles.summary: Prince William has reportedly apologised to tenants of the Bradninch Estate in Devon following a backlash over his decision to sell the 3,000-acre
articles.body: Prince William has reportedly apologised to tenants of the Bradninch Estate in Devon following a backlash over his decision to sell the 3,000-acre property, which forms part of the Duchy of Cornwall. The Prince of Wales is said to have been unhappy with reports highlighting residents' concerns about the proposed sale, with some tenants fearing they could lose their homes and livelihoods.According to a report by The Observer, William contacted the Duchy's rural director, Matthew Morris, last Sunday to discuss the growing controversy. Morris subsequently visited the estate on Thursday and met with tenants to address their concerns.During the meeting, the royal representative reportedly apologised for underestimating the time required to complete the land disposal process. He also agreed to arrange fresh independent valuations of the farms and residential properties, with the assessments to be jointly commissioned by the tenants and the Duchy.One tenant described Morris as being "all apologetic", while another reportedly welcomed the conciliatory approach but cautioned that "the proof will be in the pudding".Why Prince William's property sale has sparked backlashThe apology follows growing concerns among residents after the Duchy began the process of selling the Bradninch Estate, a 1,215-hectare (3,000-acre) property in Devon. The estate has been part of the Duchy of Cornwall since the 14th century and represents approximately one-fifth of the land portfolio William inherited from his father, King Charles III, in September 2022.The decision to sell the estate is part of William's wider plan to concentrate future Duchy investment on five geographical heartlands: the Isles of Scilly, Cornwall, Dartmoor, Bath and Kennington in south London.However, the proposed sale has caused considerable anxiety among farming and residential tenants. Last month, possession orders reportedly gave some residents just six months to either purchase their properties or leave.While tenants have been offered the opportunity to buy their homes and farms, some say the valuations are too high and do not adequately account for the money they have invested in improving the properties over the years. Others have raised concerns about their ability to afford the purchases.The controversy has also drawn criticism from Mary Ryan, a former GP who has lived in Bradninch for 36 years and is supporting affected tenants. She has accused William of hypocrisy, arguing that his commitment to tackling homelessness and mental health issues could come at the expense of rural families facing uncertainty over their own homes.Kensington Palace responds to tenants' concernsFollowing the backlash, a Kensington Palace spokesperson told The Observer that the concerns surrounding the sale were being taken seriously and that tenants were receiving individual support."We recognise that these are important and deeply personal decisions. Every tenant is being supported through the process on an individual basis, with access to practical guidance from the estate team, independent welfare and mental health support services and ongoing discussions about what is right for their circumstances," the spokesperson said.The statement also explained that the sale was part of a long-term strategy to direct future Duchy of Cornwall investment towards areas where it could deliver greater benefits for communities, farming, nature and the local economy."We will continue to support tenants with care, respect and fairness, whatever decision they ultimately make," the spokesperson added.The Duchy has also said that tenants are being offered the first opportunity to purchase their homes and farms, with discounts taking into account factors such as the length of their tenancy, the type of agreement and investments made in the properties.According to the Duchy, eight out of nine farming tenants are actively exploring the purchase of some or all of their farms, while around two-thirds of residential tenants are considering buying their homes.Questions raised over tax implications of the saleThe proposed disposal has also prompted questions about whether the Duke of Cornwall should pay capital gains tax on the proceeds.A Duchy spokesperson has maintained that the Duke is exempt because proceeds from the disposal of capital assets are required by law to be reinvested and are not available for his personal use.However, tax expert Dan Neidle has challenged that interpretation, arguing that there is no legal basis for such an exemption. He has suggested that if HM Revenue and Customs determines that capital gains tax is payable, the Duke would be required to pay it.The controversy has also reportedly disappointed King Charles, who regularly visited the Bradninch Estate when he was Prince of Wales and regarded it as an example of the rural communities that form the backbone of Britain.For now, the promise of fresh independent valuations has offered some reassurance to tenants. However, residents are still waiting to see whether the Duchy's revised approach will address their concerns over affordability, property improvements and their future on the estate.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi said India's economic growth has remained high despite the West Asia crisis, whose impact would have been far more serious if
articles.body: NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi said India's economic growth has remained high despite the West Asia crisis, whose impact would have been far more serious if the country had not invested in clean energy over the past decade.Commending India's progress in renewable energy sector, he said efforts were on to add 500GW of non-fossil energy capacity over the next 10-11 years. The PM also pitched for a "clean cooking movement" to reduce dependence on imported gas.Speaking at the inauguration of Bharat Renewable Energy Summit at Bharat Mandapam Monday, Modi said the ongoing energy crisis had underlined the link between energy security and economic security, making it imperative for countries to reduce dependence on fossil fuels."This global crisis has given every country a clear message that energy security is directly linked to economic security. If we continue to remain too dependent on fossil fuels, global economy will continue to be disrupted again and again," he said.Modi said India had already achieved nearly 300GW of non-fossil installed power capacity, accounting for more than 50% of its total capacity, and was pursuing its target of 500GW capacity by 2030.India's clean energy sector could offer investment opportunities exceeding Rs 20 lakh crore ($220 billion) by the end of the decade as the country expands renewable energy generation, transmission infrastructure, manufacturing and energy storage. More than Rs 15 lakh crore ($164 billion) had been invested in the sector over the past decade, including Rs 6 lakh crore ($63 billion) in the last two years."For all of you, a new sky of opportunities is about to open up in India's clean energy sector," he said, adding it was difficult to find "political and policy stability" like India's anywhere in the world.Referring to schemes such as PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana and PM-Kusum, Modi said India was making solar power part of citizens' lives. He called on farmers to move beyond solar pumps and become energy producers by installing panels on vacant farmland and along field boundaries. "Annadata should become Urjadata," he said.In a push to reduce dependence on imported cooking gas, Modi urged startups and innovators to develop solutions that would enable households to use rooftop solar power for cooking. articles.title: Eleições nos EUA: à espera de uma derrota, Trump ensaia o papel de 'Sr. Veto' | G1
articles.standfirst: Diante do risco de perder o controle do Congresso, presidente ameaça bloquear a agenda democrata, mas terá de enfrentar investigações e o desgaste político de seu governo.
articles.summary: Diante do risco de perder o controle do Congresso, presidente ameaça bloquear a agenda democrata, mas terá de enfrentar investigações e o desgaste político de seu governo.
articles.body:
Para quem passou os 20 meses ignorando o Congresso, o presidente Donald Trump já vislumbra a segunda metade de seu mandato sob uma nova realidade, sem o controle do Legislativo . A maioria das pesquisas aponta que os democratas terão uma vitória na Câmara e boas chances de recuperar o Senado.

A imprensa americana dá conta de que Trump traçou uma estratégia para enfrentar o pior cenário, a partir das eleições desta terça-feira — o que levaria o partido opositor a assumir o controle das duas casas do Congresso e transformá-lo em pato manco, limitando o seu poder.

O presidente antecipou a sua fórmula para governar, caso isso aconteça, e afirmou que não deixará que os democratas "estraguem tudo":

"Acho que vou me tornar o Sr. Veto", disse o presidente ao podcast "Pod Force One", do "New York Post". "Eles vão enviar algumas coisas. Você veta. E, eventualmente, depois de um ou dois meses sendo vetados, eles só estão perdendo tempo, vêm até nós e fazemos um acordo."

Em outras palavras, Trump pretende usar a caneta para assinar ordens executivas , como vem fazendo regularmente em seu segundo mandato, e vetar projetos aprovados por um Congresso controlado pela oposição .

É fácil imaginar, por exemplo, o veto do presidente em projetos prioritários dos democratas, como a reversão dos cortes na saúde e a extinção do ICE.

Donald Trump faz discurso no Memorial Lincoln, em Washington, nas vésperas das midterms — Foto: Umit Bektas/Reuters

Se os republicanos perderem o controle da Câmara dos Representantes, caberia aos democratas impor, por meio do veto, um freio à agenda da Casa Branca. Com a Câmara assegurada, o partido opositor também assumiria o controle de comissões e poderia investigar denúncias de corrupção e conflitos de interesse cometidos pelo governo e pela família do presidente.

De antemão, Trump sinalizou ainda que poderá conceder indultos preventivos para proteger assessores e aliados, entre eles o bilionário Elon Musk, caso os democratas avancem com investigações e processos judiciais.

Um terceiro pedido de impeachment de Trump, alvo de dois processos durante o primeiro mandato, não está descartado. Mas seria precipitado, pois, a exemplo dos casos anteriores, esbarraria no Senado, que precisa de maioria de dois terços para condená-lo e afastá-lo do cargo.

Na prática, Trump vem recorrendo a decretos presidenciais para levar adiante a sua agenda. Em menos de dois anos, assinou mais de 300, governando à margem do aval do Congresso: impôs tarifas a países aliados, intensificou a repressão à imigração, determinou cortes de funcionários nos departamentos e agências federais, revogou diretrizes do governo Biden sobre proteções à população LGBTQIA+, entre outras medidas.

O presidente se elegeu com promessas de conter a inflação, baixar preços e encerrar guerras, mas os americanos testemunharam o contrário disso. A guerra contra o Irã contribuiu para disparar o custo de vida e derrubou a popularidade do presidente, hoje em torno de 32% .

Quando chamou para si a disputa nas eleições de meio de mandato — "Finjam que estou na cédula", apelou aos correligionários — Trump estava convocando também um referendo sobre sua gestão. Percorreu o país e se jogou em comícios como se fosse candidato. Elevou o tom das agressões aos adversários, vangloriou-se de suas obras e passou ao largo das aflições do eleitorado. É, portanto, destinado a ele o principal recado das urnas nesta terça-feira.

Donald Trump faz discurso no Memorial Lincoln, em Washington, na véspera das midterms. — Foto: Jonathan Ernst/Reuters

articles.title: Democratas podem deportar Flávio Bolsonaro após eleições nos EUA? | G1
articles.standfirst: Brasileiros pedem nas redes a políticos democratas a deportação do senador em caso de vitória. Especialistas explicam ao g1 que eventual maioria legislativa de oposição a Trump poderia investigar e fazer pressão política, mas tirá-lo do país é mais difícil.
articles.summary: Brasileiros pedem nas redes a políticos democratas a deportação do senador em caso de vitória.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro desembarca nos EUA — Foto: Eva Marie Uzcategui/Reuters

Os Estados Unidos votam nesta terça-feira (3) nas eleições de meio de mandato (midterms), que podem mudar o equilíbrio de forças no Congresso americano e ter reflexos na permanência do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) no país.

➡️Para 2026, as projeções indicam que o Partido Democrata, que faz oposição ao presidente Donald Trump , pode reconquistar a maioria no Congresso, que hoje é dos republicanos.

Com a possibilidade de os democratas conquistarem a maioria na Câmara dos Deputados e no Senado, brasileiros têm pedido nas redes sociais que políticos do partido atuem pela deportação de Flávio, que chegou aos EUA na semana passada, após fugir do Brasil. A hashtag #DeportTheBolsonaros ficou entre as mais compartilhadas do X no Brasil nesta sexta-feira (30).

Mas como as midterms podem afetar a permanência de Flávio, aliado de Trump, no país?

Especialistas ouvidos pelo g1 apontam que a deportação ou expulsão do senador não está nas mãos do Congresso. I sso porque as decisões sobre a permanência de estrangeiros nos EUA envolvem órgãos do Executivo, como o Departamento de Estado, chefiado por Marco Rubio, e o Departamento de Segurança Interna (DHS), ambos submetidos ao governo Trump.

Mas as Casas poderiam abrir uma investigação para apurar um possível envolvimento das autoridades norte-americanas na fuga do senador brasileiro e se houve algum favorecimento na concessão de vistos para ele e sua família.

Além disso, ainda na visão dos especialistas, eventuais investigações e cobranças públicas poderiam ampliar a pressão política sobre o governo Trump e influenciar uma possível decisão das autoridades norte-americanas sobre a permanência de Flávio no país.

Apesar dessa possibilidade, a avaliação é de que a situação de Flávio não deve estar entre as prioridades dos democratas caso conquistem a maioria no Congresso.

A tendência, segundo eles, é que a oposição concentre esforços em limitar as ações de Trump, especialmente na política econômica e em questões internas, como o custo de vida da população, além de se preparar para a eleição presidencial de 2028.

O Congresso pode expulsar Flávio Bolsonaro dos EUA?

Desde a chegada de Flávio ao território norte-americano, o membro do partido democrata e comentarista político Isaiah Martin tem afirmado nas redes sociais que, com uma possível maioria democrata no Congresso, o senador seria deportado.

Contudo, como avaliam os especialistas, essa possibilidade é remota.

“Não se pode pensar que o Congresso tem o poder de deportar alguém. Isso não está na sua incumbência, não está na sua jurisdição", explica Roberto Uebel, coordenador do Núcleo de Estudos e Negócios Americanos (NENAM) e professor de Relações Internacionais da ESPM.

Vitelio Brustolin, professor no departamento de Relações Internacionais na Universidade Federal Fluminense (UFF), ressalta que a concessão ou a revogação de vistos é uma atribuição do Departamento de Estado, chefiado por Marco Rubio.

➡️O professor explica também que há diferenças entre deportação, revogação de vistos e expulsão. A revogação do visto não implica a saída automática de um estrangeiro dos EUA. Já a deportação envolve um procedimento legal para determinar sua retirada do país. A expulsão pode levar à saída obrigatória, conforme as regras migratórias aplicáveis.

Apesar disso, os democratas poderiam usar uma eventual maioria no Congresso para pressionar o governo de Trump a prestar esclarecimentos sobre a entrada e a permanência do senador brasileiro no país.

Uebel avalia que esse tipo de cobrança poderia aumentar o desgaste político do governo Trump e influenciar decisões das autoridades responsáveis pela situação migratória do senador. No entanto, ressalta que o caso brasileiro dificilmente ocupará um lugar central na agenda dos democratas.

Tomaz Paoliello, coordenador do mestrado em Governança Global e Formulação de Políticas Internacionais na Puc-SP, por sua vez, também reconhece a capacidade de pressão política do Congresso, mas considera pouco provável que ela resulte em medidas concretas contra Flávio.

“Um Congresso poderoso, a gente sabe, conhecendo a história dos EUA, consegue fazer pressão sobre as instituições burocráticas”, explica. “Particularmente, no caso do Flávio Bolsonaro, não é uma coisa tão importante - ou pelo menos eles não têm dado muita importância”, afirma.

Investigação sobre atuação do governo Trump

Uma eventual maioria democrata no Congresso poderia abrir investigações para apurar se autoridades do governo Trump ofereceram algum tipo de favorecimento a Flávio Bolsonaro e sua família. As apurações poderiam aumentar a pressão política sobre o Executivo e influenciar uma possível decisão sobre a permanência do senador no país, embora não tenham o poder de determinar sua deportação.

Segundo Brustolin, uma comissão parlamentar poderia investigar se houve tratamento excepcional na concessão de vistos, na autorização de entrada no país ou na manutenção do status migratório do senador.

“Para abrir uma investigação parlamentar basta a Câmara dos Deputados. Então não seria necessário conquistar simultaneamente maioria no Senado”, explica.

Uebel avalia que uma das principais medidas poderia ser a convocação do secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, para prestar esclarecimentos sobre a atuação do governo norte-americano no episódio.

Caso fossem identificadas irregularidades ou abusos de poder, as apurações poderiam dar origem a outras medidas contra as autoridades envolvidas, mas não teriam o poder de determinar a revogação do visto ou a saída de Flávio dos EUA.

Brustolin destaca ainda que o acesso dos parlamentares às informações migratórias não seria irrestrito. Documentos sobre vistos e comunicações do governo podem estar sujeitos a regras de confidencialidade e a questionamentos do Executivo.

“Tem também uma espécie de privilégio do Poder Executivo. A Casa Branca pode invocar privilégios e objeções legais para reter determinadas comunicações presidenciais”, explica. "Isso não cria imunidade absoluta contra investigações, mas pode provocar disputas sobre a extensão do acesso a documentos e testemunhos.”

Apesar da possibilidade de abrir investigações e pressionar o governo, os especialistas avaliam que a situação de Flávio não deve estar entre as prioridades dos democratas caso conquistem a maioria no Congresso.

Para Paoliello, as eleições de meio de mandato estão concentradas principalmente em questões internas do país, como a economia e o custo de vida da população.

O professor avalia que uma eventual maioria democrata deve dificultar a aprovação de novas leis e propostas orçamentárias do governo Trump. Ao mesmo tempo, os democratas devem buscar apresentar medidas voltadas à população, já de olho na disputa presidencial de 2028.

Roberto Uebel, por outro lado, acredita que a principal prioridade dos democratas será abrir um processo de impeachment contra Trump.

“A dúvida é se eles querem destituí-lo de fato ou arrastar um longo processo de impeachment para desgastar ao máximo o presidente Trump e os republicanos, olhando já para as eleições presidenciais de 2028”, afirma.

Paoliello discorda dessa avaliação. Segundo ele, as tentativas de destituir o presidente Trump que já ocorreram não deram um resultado político favorável aos democratas já que o republicano voltou ao poder.

🔎Trump já enfrentou dois processos de impeachment durante seu primeiro mandato. O primeiro, em 2019, envolveu acusações de abuso de poder e obstrução do Congresso após pressionar a Ucrânia a investigar Joe Biden. O segundo, em 2021, ocorreu após a invasão do Capitólio por seus apoiadores. Em ambos os casos, a Câmara aprovou o impeachment, mas o Senado absolveu o republicano.

O que disseram os democratas sobre a fuga de Flávio?

Após a chegada do senador aos EUA, um grupo de políticos democratas do Congresso questionou, em carta ao secretário de Estado Marco Rubio, o papel que o governo Trump desempenhou na fuga de Flávio e o processo de emissão de vistos para ele e sua família.

A carta, obtida pela repórter da TV Globo Raquel Krahenbuhl, foi enviada ao Departamento de Estado norte-americano na noite de quinta-feira (29).

Segundo o site norte-americano Politico, a carta é assinada por um grupo de 25 democratas da Câmara dos Deputados, liderado pelas deputadas Sydney Kamlager-Dove e Dina Titus. Entre os signatários, estão membros do Comitê de Relações Exteriores da Câmara — o órgão inclusive criticou publicamente a entrada de Flávio Bolsonaro.

"A questão central é simples: o Departamento de Estado, a Embaixada dos Estados Unidos no Brasil ou qualquer outra agência do governo americano ajudou o senador Bolsonaro a viajar para os Estados Unidos ou a entrar no país, apesar da suposta restrição judicial brasileira à sua saída?", afirmou a carta.

Apesar da mobilização, Tomaz Paoliello avalia que a situação ainda tem pouca relevância no debate eleitoral norte-americano.

"Eu acho que os democratas, nesse momento, poderiam pegar isso como uma causa se eles sentissem que isso pode impactar nas eleições", diz. "[Mas] esse tema especificamente de política externa não tem sido muito forte".

Para ele, isso se dá porque as eleições para o Congresso focam mais em questões internas dos EUA do que a posição de Trump em relação a outros países.

O que dizem as pesquisas sobre as midterms?

Pesquisas e projeções recentes indicam que os democratas podem conquistar a maioria do Senado nas eleições de novembro.

articles.title: O caminho dos R$ 816 mil: como foi pago o voo de Flávio Bolsonaro aos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Dono da companhia aérea afirmou que dinheiro saiu de uma conta empresarial americana e foi transferido para banco argentino. Apesar de imprensa apontar participação de assessor de Trump na organização da viagem, não se sabe quem bancou o voo.
articles.summary: Dono da companhia aérea afirmou que dinheiro saiu de uma conta empresarial americana e foi transferido para banco argentino. Apesar de imprensa apontar participação de assessor de Trump na organização da viagem, não se sabe quem bancou o voo.
articles.body:
O voo que levou o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e sua família da Argentina aos Estados Unidos custou US$ 150 mil (cerca de R$ 816 mil) e foi pago por um intermediário do setor de aviação que mora em território americano. A identidade de quem contratou a viagem, porém, não foi esclarecida.

Uma reportagem do Fantástico , exibida neste domingo (1º), apresentou detalhes da operação montada para a saída do senador do Brasil, incluindo informações sobre o pagamento do jato de luxo que transportou Flávio, a mulher, Fernanda, e as duas filhas do casal.

O avião utilizado foi um Gulfstream G400, de prefixo LV-JQW, operado pela companhia argentina Baires Fly, que pertence ao empresário Luis Grande.

Em entrevista à agência France-Presse (AFP), Grande revelou que o dinheiro saiu de uma conta empresarial em um banco americano e foi transferido para uma instituição bancária argentina.

Segundo ele, pagamento foi realizado por um intermediário do setor de aviação que mora nos Estados Unidos . O empresário, no entanto, não revelou o nome dessa pessoa e afirmou desconhecer a identidade do contratante final do voo.

Embora o proprietário da Baires Fly não tenha identificado quem contratou a aeronave, a imprensa americana apontou que Jason Miller, assessor do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, teria sido responsável por providenciar a viagem de Flávio Bolsonaro.

Flávio e seu irmão, Eduardo Bolsonaro, estiveram com Miller nos Estados Unidos quando o senador ainda era pré-candidato à Presidência da República.

A reportagem também citou uma publicação do jornal argentino Clarín, segundo a qual agentes americanos teriam assumido o controle de parte do aeroporto de Puerto Iguazú, na Argentina, durante a operação de saída do senador.

O secretário de Estado americano, Marco Rubio, negou que o governo dos Estados Unidos tenha colaborado com a saída de Flávio do Brasil.

"Não facilitamos nada. Não tivemos nenhuma participação nos preparativos que ele fez. O governo dos Estados Unidos não teve participação direta em nenhuma das movimentações realizadas", declarou Rubio.

O voo partiu de Puerto Iguazú, cidade argentina vizinha a Foz do Iguaçu, no Paraná, que possui um aeroporto internacional com pista de 3.300 metros, capaz de receber grandes jatos executivos.

Segundo a reportagem do Fantástico, a operação para levar Flávio e sua família até o aeroporto argentino envolveu diferentes trajetos.

Uma das versões apuradas aponta que o senador teria deixado Brasília na manhã de terça-feira (27), em um avião ligado ao advogado Willer Tomaz, e desembarcado em San Fernando, na região de Buenos Aires. De lá, teria seguido em outro voo privado para Puerto Iguazú.

Já Fernanda e as duas filhas teriam viajado de Brasília até Cascavel, no Paraná, antes de seguirem de van para a Argentina.

Apesar de os registros migratórios argentinos indicarem uma entrada terrestre de Flávio no país, a principal linha de investigação aponta que ele teria chegado a Puerto Iguazú de avião e permanecido por horas dentro da aeronave à espera da família.

A assessoria de Willer Tomaz negou que uma aeronave pertencente a ele ou a empresas vinculadas à sua família tenha sido utilizada pelo senador ou seus familiares para deixar o Brasil.

Depois de reunir a família em Puerto Iguazú, o jato da Baires Fly seguiu para os Estados Unidos, com uma escala em Guayaquil, no Equador, para reabastecimento.

Flávio, Fernanda e as duas filhas desembarcaram na manhã de quarta-feira (28), no Aeroporto Executivo de Opa-Locka, na região de Miami, na Flórida.

A saída do aeroporto foi acompanhada por helicópteros de emissoras americanas, enquanto os carros que transportavam a família seguiram com escolta policial. O acompanhamento terminou na região de Pembroke Pines, mas o destino final da família não foi confirmado.

Flávio deixou o Brasil após o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) determinar que ele entregasse seus passaportes à Polícia Federal.

Procurada pelo Fantástico, a Baires Fly não respondeu aos questionamentos. Já o advogado Frederick Wassef, representante legal de Flávio Bolsonaro, afirmou que nenhuma informação sobre a viagem do senador era oficial ou havia sido confirmada. Ele também negou que a saída do país tenha sido uma fuga.

articles.title: iPhone Duo: Apple unsure when more of the foldable devices will be available
articles.summary: Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo was a hit with people willing to spend $2,000 on a new mobile.
articles.body:
The new head of Apple says the company is working to get its new foldable iPhones available to more people after the $1,999 smartphone quickly sold out when it was released just over a week ago.

John Ternus, who in September took over the role as Apple's chief executive from Tim Cook, said on Monday that he was "thrilled" at the early reaction to the iPhone Duo.

While the costly phone, which sells for £1,999 in the UK, immediately sold out, some buyers have seen their screens crack .

The phones are still in high demand and Sabhi Kahn, Apple's new chief operating officer, said the technology giant did not know when more Duos would be available.

"At this time, it's really hard to predict when supply and demand will be in balance," Kahn said during a call with financial analysts to discuss Apple's latest financial results.

Apple executives did not mention during the call any issues with the iPhone Duo. But last week, the company said it would replace any phones that were impacted by an issue that caused a "small number" of the new phones to crack along the inside fold.

Nevertheless, Apple said on Monday that over the last year it sold more iPhones globally than it ever has before.

During the three months to 26 September, which did not include sales of the iPhone Duo that went on sale toward the end of October, Apple saw iPhone sales rise 17% to $57bn.

Apple has boasted throughout the year that iPhone sales have been surging, despite the company's warnings that crucial components for the device, along with Mac computers and iPads, were constrained to the point of weighing down sales.

Sales of Mac computers also grew during the quarter by 27%, hitting $10.7bn, another record for Apple.

Overall sales at the company rose by 15% for the year, to $479bn.

However, sales for both the iPad and Apple's wearable products, including its headphones and Watch fell by 10% and 7%, respectively.

Kahn noted during the call that most Apple devices are still seeing supply constraints driven in part by difficulty in getting enough microprocessors with "advanced nodes."

Those components are essentially computer chip technology that allows Apple's devices to operate more quickly, most of which Apple has manufactured through TSMC, which is based in Taiwan.

Khan said that such supply constraints are expected to continue into next year, particularly impacting iPads and Macs. The situation has been made worse by what the company has repeatedly insisted is "unexpected demand" for its products.

Ternus noted, too, that Apple is still seeing "unprecedented" cost increases for memory, or the ability of Apple devices to store data like apps, photos, and text messages.

Much of that memory storage runs through data centres which have seen a huge boom in demand for space as artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots and platforms, including those developed by OpenAI and Anthropic, have become popular.

As demand for memory has grown, storage prices have gone up for tech companies like Apple.

Cook had earlier this year referred to the sudden increase in data centre costs that Apple was seeing as a "thousand year flood."

It has led to the company raising prices on essentially all of its hardware products by around 20%.

articles.title: Four states vote Tuesday on ballot measures that could reshape girls' and women's sports nationwide
articles.summary: Voters in Arizona, Nebraska, Washington and Colorado face Tuesday ballot measures on transgender athletes in girls sports and locker room policies.
articles.body: Four states have measures on Tuesday's ballot that could change who gets to compete in girls' and women's sports — and, in some cases, who gets to use their locker rooms. Arizona and Nebraska already have laws restricting biological males from competing in female sports. A "yes" vote in either state would expand or strengthen those existing restrictions. Washington and Colorado are different. Neither currently has the statewide sex-based restrictions proposed by these measures. If voters approve them, both states would establish statewide sex-based restrictions for school sports — a significant change in two traditionally Democratic states. WHERE TOP DEMOCRAT SENATE CANDIDATES AND THEIR GOP OPPONENTS STAND ON TRANS ATHLETES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS So what's at stake Tuesday? Here's a state-by-state breakdown of what the measures would do, what opponents are saying, how supporters are responding and what the betting markets are predicting. Washington: Initiative 638 What a yes vote would do: Prohibit students defined as biologically male from competing in girls' K-12 interscholastic sports. Girls seeking to participate would have to provide documentation from a healthcare professional verifying biological sex based on "reproductive anatomy, genetic makeup, or normal endogenously produced testosterone levels." As it stands, K-12 athletes in Washington can compete based on their gender identity under current eligibility rules, which allowed a boy in Camas, WA, to switch to the girls' team mid-season earlier this year. What a no vote would do: Keep the current eligibility rules in place, without adding the initiative's new sex-verification requirements. What opponents say: Organizations such as No Hate in Washington State argue that the initiative would discriminate against transgender students and could subject girls to invasive genital examinations. NEW POLL SHOWS WASHINGTON STATE VOTERS ARE READY TO END BOYS COMPETING IN GIRLS' SPORTS Proponents call the "invasive exam" argument fearmongering, saying that biological sex can be verified as part of a routine sports physical — something high school athletes have been undergoing for years. They also point to a simple cheek swab, which collects DNA from inside the mouth, as another possible way to verify biological sex. Polymarket prediction at the time of writing: 64% market-implied probability of I-638 passing. Colorado: Proposition 134 What a yes vote would do: Establish statewide sex-based participation requirements for school sports from K-12 through the college level. Athletes would generally compete on teams matching their biological sex, with exceptions for coed sports and girls joining boys' teams when no equivalent girls' team exists. The measure covers public, charter and private schools, as well as colleges and universities. It applies to interscholastic and intramural athletics, including school-sponsored club sports. Proposition 134 defines females as "a person whose biological reproductive system is organized around the production of ova" and males as "a person whose biological reproductive system is organized around the production of sperm." Unlike Washington's initiative, Colorado's measure doesn't specifically require a doctor's note or medical examination to verify biological sex. Instead, schools would have to establish their own eligibility policies, with no verification method specified in the measure. The state education commissioner could take action against school districts that intentionally refuse to comply. What a no vote would do: Maintain the existing eligibility system, allowing schools, districts and athletic associations to continue setting their own participation policies, subject to state and federal law. What opponents say: Planned Parenthood and other opponents echo the concerns raised in Washington, arguing that Proposition 134 amounts to government overreach and "risks invasive gender checks for girls." But as XX-XY Athletics founder Jennifer Sey — who chairs the campaign supporting Proposition 134 — has pointed out, 27 states already have restrictions on biological males competing in girls' sports. Sey argues that the invasive examinations opponents warn about aren't happening in those states. Polymarket prediction at the time of writing: 55% market-implied probability of Proposition 134 passing. Arizona: Proposition 318 What a yes vote would do: Build on Arizona's existing public school sports rules by expanding restrictions to private schools and athletic associations, including those overseeing youth and college sports. It would also require schools and athletic associations to restrict access to restrooms, locker rooms and other private spaces connected to athletics based on biological sex as recorded on an original birth certificate. The measure would also allow athletes to sue schools and athletic associations that knowingly violate the law. It would retain protections for athletes competing on coed teams and would not categorically prohibit girls from participating on boys' teams. What a no vote would do: Leave existing laws in place, keeping Arizona's current public school sports restrictions without expanding them to additional institutions or adding the measure's new requirements for private spaces. What opponents say: Civil rights groups such as the ACLU argue that Proposition 318 singles out transgender students, could subject girls to intrusive questioning about their biological sex and opens schools up to expensive lawsuits. Supporters counter that the measure closes loopholes in existing law, protects privacy and safety in locker rooms and bathrooms, and establishes consistent rules for fair athletic competition across the state. Polymarket prediction at the time of writing: 82% market-implied probability of Proposition 318 passing. SUPREME COURT MAKES RULING ON TRANS ATHLETES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Nebraska: Initiative 442 What a yes vote would do: Amend Nebraska's Constitution to prohibit biological males from competing in girls' and women's school sports, from K-12 through college. Schools would have to designate teams as male, female or coed, with female teams reserved for biological females. The measure would apply to public schools and colleges, as well as private institutions whose teams compete against public schools. Unlike Washington and Colorado, Nebraska already has a law restricting biological males from competing in girls' and women's sports. Gov. Jim Pillen signed the Stand With Women Act in June 2025. Arizona also has an existing law, but Nebraska's ballot measure would go a step further by putting its restrictions into the state constitution, making them harder for future lawmakers to overturn. What a no vote would do: Leave Nebraska's Constitution unchanged. The existing law restricting biological males from competing in girls' and women's sports would remain in effect. What opponents say: Groups such as OutNebraska and the Fairness for All campaign argue that the amendment would discriminate against transgender students and unnecessarily write restrictions into the state constitution when a law already exists. Opponents also point out that transgender athletes make up a tiny percentage of the state's population. Supporters counter that putting the restrictions into the constitution would protect female athletes from future changes to state law. The Fairness for Girls campaign argues that allowing biological males to compete against girls creates safety concerns and can cost female athletes medals, advancement opportunities and scholarships. articles.title: 17-year-old arrested in Spirit Halloween shooting that killed pregnant woman, injured 6 other people
articles.summary: The attack took place Friday as shoppers at the store in the San Francisco Bay Area city of Fairfield prepared for Halloween.
articles.body: A 17-year-old boy has been arrested in last week’s shooting at a Spirit Halloween store in California that killed a pregnant woman and injured six other people, police said Monday. The suspect, whose name will not be released because he is a minor, will be charged with one count of murder but could face an additional murder count because 31-year-old victim Constance Hages was pregnant, Fairfield Police Chief Dan Marshall said. The teen was arrested in Suisun City, a municipality adjacent to Fairfield, where the shooting took place at Solano Town Center mall around 8:30 p.m. Friday, police said at a news conference Monday. A 16-year-old boy and two men, ages 19 and 32, were left in critical condition, Marshall said. A 23-year-old man was stable in critical condition at a hospital, and two other men, ages 19 and 43, were treated for gunshot wounds and later released, according to authorities. All but one of the victims still hospitalized Monday had been stabilized, with one still in critical condition, Marshall said. The shooter entered the store and targeted someone specific inside when he opened fire, said Officer Michelle Belyea, a police spokesperson. Marshall said that the shooter used a handgun and that there may have been a previous altercation between him and a victim. The suspect opened fire on a vehicle at a local high school last year and was in custody for a few months as a result, Marshall said. He bemoaned what he characterized as a lack of accountability in that case. “This event shouldn’t have even occurred,” Marshall said. “California has gotten extremely soft on accountability with youth.” He said detectives identified a suspect hours after the attack but didn’t want to tip him off. The teen was arrested at his home Monday afternoon, Marshall said. The suspect is believed to have acted alone, he said. Fairfield, a city of more than 122,000, is about 45 miles northeast of San Francisco.

articles.title: US lawmakers ask Trump administration to stop deportation of Afghans
articles.summary: At least 150 Afghans are facing deportation to Pakistan and on to Afghanistan.
articles.body:
A group of 66 lawmakers in the United States has written to the administration of President Donald Trump asking it to halt a planned mass deportation of Afghans, including some who worked alongside coalition forces in Afghanistan before the military withdrawal in 2021.

In Monday’s letter, the lawmakers cited advocacy group reports that at least 150 Afghans were scheduled to be deported from Tuesday – flown from detention facilities in Louisiana to Pakistan.

The Associated Press news agency also reported that Department of Homeland Security (DHS) officials had said in court filings that they eventually planned on returning some of the Afghans to their home country.

The US does not have diplomatic relations with Afghanistan, which has been governed by the Taliban since US troops withdrew in August 2021.

“Sending dozens of people back to one of the most dangerous countries on earth, and where they are likely to be targeted for their or their family’s suspected support of the US government or criticism of the Taliban, is a death sentence,” the lawmakers wrote in the letter addressed to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin.

“Our country made a promise never to abandon the Afghans who sacrificed their own and their family’s safety to stand with American service members.”

As part of its crackdown on immigration, the Trump administration has made agreements with at least 35 countries to take in third-country nationals , in many cases because it cannot send them back to their home countries for fear they would be tortured, killed, or otherwise persecuted.

Critics of the practice have said it undermines decades of global humanitarian norms around asylum seeker and refugee protection. They say deportees often end up in countries with a record of human rights abuses, or places that are so dangerous the US tells its own citizens not to travel there.

The Trump administration has forcibly sent at least 25,000 people to third countries, according to a tally by nonprofits Refugees International and Human Rights First.

Human Rights First said it has confirmed that a flight carrying some of the Afghans from Alexandria, Louisiana, to Pakistan is scheduled for Tuesday.

Rights advocates say the batch of deportations to Pakistan may also include Iranians, small numbers of whom the Trump administration has previously sent to third countries to eventually be returned to Iran, despite the ongoing war the US is waging on the country.

Pakistan has deported millions of Afghans to Afghanistan in recent years, as relations with the Taliban have deteriorated.

Most of the Afghans scheduled for deportation did not have the opportunity to properly fight their removal in court, Shawn VanDiver, founder and president of the AfghanEvac advocacy group, said.

“They were placed into removal proceedings because they didn’t have attorneys to fight,” he said.

VanDiver said he spoke to one man on Monday, a former police officer in the Afghan government toppled by the Taliban, who expected to be deported and feared for his life if he ended up back in Afghanistan. Others, VanDiver said, had also either worked in the Afghan government or with the US, or had family that did so, and would be in danger in Afghanistan.

Since taking office, Trump has attempted to put an end to resettlement programmes for Afghans started by former President Joe Biden. More than 120,000 Afghans were evacuated from Afghanistan in 2021 after the chaotic withdrawal of US forces.

Some ended up in facilities abroad, like in Qatar. This September, the US granted a nine-month extension for Camp As Sayliyah, a facility in Qatar housing more than 1,000 Afghans who assisted US forces in Afghanistan.

Afghans evacuated to the US were initially granted humanitarian parole, allowing them to stay in the country. In 2022, the Biden administration granted them Temporary Protected Status for 18 months, allowing them to live and work legally in the US after their parole period expired, and while their immigration status was resolved.

But since then, few Afghans in the US have been able to move their applications for asylum, or other special protected status relating to their work with coalition forces, through the severely backlogged immigration system.

“These people are in dire straits; they have been stuck in this limbo for five years, waiting for permanency, waiting for green cards, waiting to hear about their status,” VanDiver said.

The Trump administration has instituted record-low quotas for asylum applications globally. However, he made an exception for white Afrikaners from South Africa, giving them sanctuary after alleging they had faced racial discrimination against white people.

Trump ordered a halt to processing applications from Afghans after a man from Afghanistan allegedly shot two National Guardsmen in Washington, DC, in November 2025. The Trump administration also included Afghan nationals in a blanket visa ban earlier this year, saying it would review immigration applications filed by anyone from the country. Both policies were challenged in court.

VanDiver said he and other advocates have been pushing for new legislation that would provide Afghans protection in the US, including a bill – co-sponsored by both Republican and Democratic lawmakers – that would grant many Temporary Protected Status after the Trump administration withdrew it.
